item.title: FOB China TOPCon solar cell prices hold steady as market awaits post-holiday reassessment
item.description: In a new weekly update for pv magazine, OPIS, a Dow Jones company, provides a quick look at the main price trends in the global PV industry.

item.title: Greece to open applications for 130 MW agrivoltaics plan
item.description: Greece’s distribution grid operator will begin accepting applications for agrivoltaic systems on March 4, marking the first step in implementing a new law targeting 130 MW of capacity nationwide.

item.title: Tropical downpours cut northern irradiance as southern heat lifts sunshine in South America
item.description: In a new weekly update for pv magazine, Solcast, a DNV company, reports that January in South America featured dramatic weather contrasts with persistent floods and cloud cover in northern regions sharply reducing solar irradiance, while extreme heat, drought and wildfires in the south boosted sunlight yet also generated aerosol smoke that complicated irradiance outcomes. item.title: ‘Like many people, I’ve been the only woman in the room’
item.description: This week Women in Solar+ Europe gives voice to Charmaine Coutinho, Director - EMEA Energy Transition at UK-based FTI Consulting. She says the energy transition requires inclusive systems that actively involve underrepresented groups, ensuring diversity and equity at all levels. Drawing on decades in the sector, she emphasizes intentional mentorship, sponsorship, and transparent leadership as essential for meaningful change and career impact.

item.title: Philippines mandates energy storage for renewables plants over 10 MW
item.description: Department of Energy (DOE) order sets out new rules for mandatory energy storage, including a minimum capacity of at least 20% of the generating plant’s installed capacity. DOE also calls forenergy storage systems (ESS) installations to have grid supporting capabilities, such as grid-forming inverters to help stabilize voltage and frequency.

item.title: The richest silver mine isn’t underground but in solar
item.description: As primary silver grades decline and solar demand surges, the industry must transition from viewing retired panels as waste to treating them as high-grade mineral reserves essential for the energy transition.

item.title: Global energy transition hits a hardware bottleneck
item.description: As transformer lead times double and US prices surge 79%, a manufacturing “supercycle” struggles to keep pace with the explosive growth of AI data centers and renewable energy.

item.title: Bluetti launching Elite 300, world’s smallest 3 kWh portable power station
item.description: The Bluetti Elite 300, packing more power than ever into a small form, will be available with early-bird discounts from March 8.

item.title: The Hydrogen Stream: ACES 220 MW Utah project nears completion
item.description: HydrogenPro says its 220 MW ACES Delta project in Utah is nearing completion, with all electrolyzers operating at full load, while the hub will store hydrogen in salt caverns with energy capacity two to three times that of all US grid-connected batteries combined.

item.title: India expected to install about 42.5 GW of new solar capacity in 2026
item.description: India installed around 37.8 GW of solar capacity in 2025, according to JKM Research. This comprised about 28.6 GW of new utility-scale solar, a 54.6% increase from 2024, and 7.9 GW of rooftop solar, up 72% year on year. Off-grid additions stood at 1.35 GW, compared to 1.48 GW in 2024.
